series_key: developing an mqtt client for metatrader 5: a tdd approach —
idea_name: MQTT CONNECT packet TDD scaffolding only
mechanism: Builds Defines.mqh/MQTT.mqh enums, IControlPacket, and CPktConnect Fixed/Variable Header (protocol name MQTT, level 0x05, Connect Flags, Keep Alive, Client Identifier) with fixture byte-array unit tests against Mosquitto; no market features.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing after full read—protocol client engineering only.
quote: The single purpose of the CPktConnect class is to build a well-formed MQTT CONNECT packet.

series_key: developing an mqtt client for metatrader 5: a tdd approach —
idea_name: MQTT Connect Flags and CONNACK Reason Code handling only
mechanism: Implements Clean Start/Will/QoS/Retain/UserName/Password bit flags, CSrvResponse.GetPktType/GetConnectReasonCode, and Server Profile stub for QoS/Retain-not-supported; Operational Behavior of MQTT, not markets.
why_new_for_mis: No market regime/vol/liquidity sensor—broker capability negotiation only.
quote: from now on we need to deal with the packets sent from the server. Our client must be able to identify the server packet type

series_key: developing an mqtt client for metatrader 5: a tdd approach —
idea_name: MQTT v5 Properties and User-Property extensibility only
mechanism: Documents CONNACK/PUBLISH property identifiers, Variable Byte Integer decode, HasProperties/GetPropertyIdentifier readers, and an illustrative User Property for signal_provider:provider_broker symbol aliasing (GOLD/XAUUSD)—integration metadata, not a market sensor.
data_needed: none for sensing; optional User Property key-value pairs for routing
why_new_for_mis: Full read yields protocol extensibility and signal-routing metadata, not MIS sensing of regime/vol/liquidity.
quote: Properties are part of the ‘extensibility mechanisms’ that were added in MQTT v5.0.

series_key: developing an mqtt client for metatrader 5: a tdd approach —
idea_name: MQTT PUBLISH Fixed Header flags and Topic Name encoding only
mechanism: Implements PUBLISH RETAIN/QoS/DUP flags, UTF-8 Topic Name with disallowed-codepoint and wildcard guards, and QoS>0 Packet Identifier assignment; messaging protocol core, not price sensing.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing—PUBLISH packet construction under TDD.
quote: MQTT is a pub/sub message sharing protocol. So we can expect that its core is on PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE packets.

series_key: developing an mqtt client for metatrader 5: a tdd approach —
idea_name: MQTT CPublish Build/PUBACK and fake persistence only
mechanism: Refactors order-independent CPublish setters + Build(), property encoders, CPuback GetPacketID/IsPendingPkt against GetPendingPublishIDs fixture; Session State deferred to SQLite later—still protocol plumbing.
why_new_for_mis: No market sensing—TDD refactor and PUBACK acknowledgment path only.
quote: Continuous refactoring is part of TDD practice.

idea_name: Fixed-width fractional differentiation (FFD) stationary memory-preserving feature sensor
mechanism: Apply binomial weights ω0=1, ωk=−ωk−1(d−k+1)/k truncated when |ω| < τ (default 1e−5) as a fixed lookback window; each bar is a dot product of that constant weight vector with log-prices (or other series), yielding a driftless stationary series that still tracks level/structure of the original. Prefer FFD over expanding-window fracdiff which accumulates negative-drift artifacts.
data_needed: Price (or other non-stationary) series; d and τ; optional use_log=True before differencing; first l* bars discarded until window fills.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic GBM demo; cited across 87 liquid futures; pipeline inputs include close, VWAP, volume, cumulative volumes, microstructural features on bar data (timeframe unspecified).
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a principled alternative to raw returns: a bounded-lookback, streamable transform that keeps long-memory level information while satisfying ML stationarity—usable as the front-end feature for any downstream regime/vol model.
quote: The fixed-width window (FFD) method is the production-grade variant: it applies a constant, precomputed weight vector across the entire series, producing a driftless, stationary output that preserves the maximum possible memory from the original price process.

idea_name: Minimum d* via ADF binary search as stationarity–memory operating point
mechanism: Binary-search d in [0, max_d] (default 1): at midpoint compute FFD, run ADF (maxlag=1, regression=c); if stationary (adfStat < 5% critical and pVal < alpha) lower high, else raise low; stop when high−low < tol (~1e−3, ~10 iters). Return FFD series at smallest passing d* plus ADF table and corr(original, FFD).
data_needed: Series ≥~100 non-NaN FFD points; ADF critical values; optional cache of evaluated d.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same as FFD demos; López de Prado note that 87 liquid futures all reached stationarity with d < 0.6.
why_new_for_mis: Automates the least-destructive differentiation order so MIS features are stationary without the systematic over-differentiation of d=1 returns.
quote: the optimal d* is the smallest value that crosses the stationarity threshold. This is a root-finding problem, and binary search is the natural algorithm.

mechanism: Alongside ADF, compute corrcoef between original (log-)prices and FFD series at each candidate d; correlation near 1 at low d and falling toward 0 at d=1 quantifies memory retained. Operate at the d* where ADF just passes while correlation remains high (article example crossing near d*≈0.15).
data_needed: Aligned original and FFD series at shared index; ADF row per d.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic/log-price demos; futures universe cited for d*<0.6.
why_new_for_mis: Turns the stationarity–memory tradeoff into an explicit MIS diagnostic: reject transforms that buy stationarity by destroying level memory.
quote: This correlation measures memory preservation — the closer to 1.0, the more of the original series' structure survives the transformation.

idea_name: Cached d* shift as memory-structure / regime-break sensor
mechanism: Persist per-asset, per-timeframe optimal d*; reuse across runs. Recompute when data changes materially—article states d* moves only when the price process memory structure shifts (regime changes, structural breaks). A material jump in re-estimated d* is itself a change signal.
data_needed: Historical bars for periodic fracdiff_optimal; stored d* cache keyed by asset/timeframe.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Per asset and timeframe (unspecified bars); futures/price processes generally.
why_new_for_mis: Elevates the fractional order from a static hyperparameter to a meta-sensor of regime/structural change in memory dynamics.
quote: The d* value is stable for a given asset and timeframe — it changes only when the memory structure of the price process shifts materially (regime changes, structural breaks).

idea_name: FFD overlay as level/trend/regime-tracking stationary path
mechanism: Plot/compare FFD(d≈0.4) against raw prices: FFD oscillates around a stable mean while visibly tracking trends, regime changes, and relative levels of the original—usable as a regime-aware state feature where returns would erase that path.
data_needed: Paired price and FFD series at chosen d.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic GBM illustration; general price bars.
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS a stationary path feature that still encodes where price sits relative to recent structure—supporting mean-reversion and trend regime logic without cointegration fragility.
quote: Trends, regime changes, and relative levels are visibly tracked by the FFD series.

mechanism: López de Prado four-step: (1) cumulative sum of the series (forces a unit root even if already stationary), (2) FFD over d∈[0,1], (3) minimum d with ADF p<5%, (4) use FFD(d*) as predictive feature—automated by fracdiff_optimal. Apply to each non-stationary raw feature (prices, cumulative volumes, running sums) before model training; verify full matrix with is_stationary.
data_needed: Raw feature columns; ADF alpha; fixed_width=True default.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Bar-data features: close, VWAP, volume, microstructural; any timeframe once bar series exists.
why_new_for_mis: Standardizes MIS feature ingress so every level-like channel is stationarized with maximal memory before neural/sequence sensors see it.
quote: Compute the cumulative sum of the time series. This ensures that some order of differentiation is needed, even if the original series is already stationary — the cumsum introduces a unit root.

idea_name: Streaming FFD engine with precomputed weights and bounded lookback
mechanism: Precompute weight vector once for fixed (d, τ); each new bar needs only CopyClose/lookback of l*+1 values and an O(l*) dot product—compatible with streaming MT5 (follow-up MQL5 article). Weight vector reusable indefinitely for same d,τ.
data_needed: Static ω array; rolling window of l*+1 closes (or feature values).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Live MetaTrader 5 feeds (planned MQL5 port); bar count ~10k with window ~100 in Python timing note.
why_new_for_mis: Makes fractional-diff sensing operational for live MIS rather than batch-only research transforms.
quote: Each observation depends only on a bounded lookback window, making it compatible with streaming architectures.

series_key: implementing practical modules from other languages in mql5
idea_name: Python-like REQUESTS HTTP client wrapper only
mechanism: CSession/CResponse wrap WebRequest with get/post/put/patch/delete_, JSON/form headers, multipart file upload, cookies, Basic Auth, BuildUrlWithParams—HTTP plumbing for MT5, no market feature construction.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: none (httpbin.org / tmpfiles.org demos; chart.jpg upload example)
why_new_for_mis: Full read is an HTTP convenience library inspired by Python requests—no regime/vol/liquidity/neural sensing.
quote: In this article, we are going to implement a similar module with similar functions, syntax, and capabilities. Hoping to make it easy and convenient to perform webrequests in MQL5 as in Python.
